title: Life cycle of deep convection in climate models
author: Arthur Guy Furtado Colfort
abstract: Using work developed during the final year stage of the study, on the detection and analysis of the representation of deep convective systems in global circulation climate models, a statistical approach is used to develop correlations, calculate biases, and compare the models with observational data. of satellite. The two global climate models are developed in the CNRM laboratory, Center National des Recherches Météorologiques, in France, where the internship takes place. First, an overview of the literature on mesoscale systems is presented, followed by the development of a definition of deep convective events suitable for the convective systems produced by the models, and then the detection algorithm explained. Satellite data comes from geostationary observations in the infrared range that are handled by a mesoscale system detection algorithm that generates the database of deep convective systems detected over time. The area of interest is located between the tropics, where deep convective activity is more pronounced. The characterization of deep convective events is then developed and comparisons between the models and the satellite observation data are made. The comparison between the fluid dynamics parameterizations of the two models is also developed in order to analyze the influence of each block of parameterizations on the behavior of variables in a deep convective system.
